subject: Yoruba
sourceFile: Copy of Yoruba BECE Syllabus - syllabusNG.txt
examFormat: Based on the 9-year Basic Education Curriculum for Yoruba, for candidates who speak Yoruba as a first language (L1) or second language (L2); it tests the ability to read, write and comprehend Yoruba, construct sentences correctly with idiomatic expressions, show familiarity with Yoruba culture, read and appreciate literature, write essays and short stories and translate simple sentences from English to Yoruba. L1 has two papers of 60 multiple-choice questions each (120 in all): Paper 1 covers grammar (25), comprehension (10), composition (5), sound system (10), orthography (5) and translation (5); Paper 2 covers oral literature (15), prose (5), drama (5), poetry (5) and culture and tradition (20). L2 is one 1-hour paper of 60 multiple-choice questions in sections A-D: dialogue (10), written comprehension (10), numbers, greetings, alphabets, translation, grammar and culture (25), and pictures of time, the human body, animals, crops, utensils and school-related items (15).
excluded: syllabus.ng 'About us', 'About BECE', eligibility, grading, registration and FAQ chapters. The L1 and L2 syllabuses are combined in this one file; L2 topic names are suffixed '(L2)'. The extraction corrupted Yoruba tone marks and under-dots (stray characters such as å, ö, ΀), so Yoruba is written without diacritics and with clear OCR errors corrected; this makes 'aroko' (essay, Language IV) and 'aroko' (coded message, Culture XIV, heading missing in the text) look alike, so they are named 'Aroko oniroyin' and 'Aroko ati ipaaroko'. L2 Literature I and III share the heading 'Alo ati orin keekeeke' and are qualified; L2 Culture has two topics numbered XII. Some place/name readings are uncertain (e.g. 'Igba Ibolo' read as 'Igbo Ora', 'Sibee' as 'Sabe').
